newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr/yen's downside seen limited in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen's downside seen limited in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to consolidate its bottom at around 118.00 yen or just below that point on Thursday, after failing an attempt to penetrate 119 yen overnight, dealers said.

Expectations that Japan's low interest rates will continue for a while after Japan's weak industrial output data on Wednesday and a surge in U.S. stocks to record-high levels could support underlying strength in the dollar, they said.
"It's likely to consolidate its bottom and then resume rising towards 119 yen today," said a trust bank dealer. The bottom could be supported at around 117.70 yen, he added.
The trust bank dealer said U.S. funds operators, a main driving force of the dollar's rally in recent trade, are expected to keep buying dollars on dips.
"Their buying was so aggressive (on Wednesday) that selling by Japanese operators only put a brief brake on the dollar's rise," he added.
The dollar rose as high as 118.95 yen overnight on Wednesday, but later retreated due to renewed concerns about U.S.-Japan trade relations.
Traders in New York cited rumours that U.S. car markers wanted Washington to review U.S.-Japan trade barriers.
Dealers said hedge selling by Japanese pension funds on rises and stronger selling orders by Japanese exporters above 119.00 yen could limit the dollar's rise today.

"Exporters are still willing to sell dollars, but the fact is that buying demand is outpacing selling interest," said a Japanese city bank dealer."So I don't think the dollar's recent rally is over, there could be further scope to rise," he added.
He said market attention is shifting to dollar/yen trade from dollar/mark, adding that the dollar is likely to hover between 1.8300 and 1.8400 marks in Asia.
